abstract: We construct the largest $r$-flower-free system of $k$-uniform sets for $k=3, r=4$ where every element of the ground set $G$ is used at least once. The goal is to maximize $|G|$, also called the span. We define $\mathrm{sp}(k, r)$ to be the maximum $|G|$ for such a system. We show that $\mathrm{sp}(3, 4) = 39$, which yields an improved upper bound $f(3, 4) \leq 130$, improving upon the Erd\H{o}s--Rado bound of $f(3, 4) \leq 162$.
hook: The largest ground set for 4-sunflower-free triple systems is 39, tightening a bound from 162 to 130
summary: For systems of 3-element sets with no 4-petal sunflower, the paper shows the maximum ground-set size (span) is exactly 39. This lowers the upper bound f(3,4) from the Erdos-Rado value of 162 to 130. It settles only the case k=3, r=4.
title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems
